Milking machine collects milk (twice a day)

Milk tanker delivers milk to the dairy daily

Products distributed to supermarkets, shops and convenience stores

The diagram illustrates the sequence of stages involved in producing milk and milk-based products, from the farm to the shop shelf.

Overall, the process begins with cows grazing outdoors and ends with a range of dairy products being distributed to retail outlets, with the raw milk being split into two separate production lines partway through.

At the first stage, cows graze in the field before being brought in twice a day to be milked by machine. The raw milk collected is then transferred to refrigerated storage tanks to keep it fresh. From there, a tanker transports the milk to the dairy on a daily basis for processing.

Once at the dairy, the milk supply divides into two separate streams. A portion is used to manufacture cheese, cream and butter, while the remainder undergoes pasteurisation before being packaged as bottled milk. In the final stage, both the pasteurised milk and the other dairy products are distributed to supermarkets, smaller shops and convenience stores, ready for consumers to purchase.
